clue.text: Commander-in-Chief realising some changes are necessary

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the two preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A top commander admits that some reforms must be made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the thirteen letters of REALISING and SOME; 'are necessary' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A generalissimo is the supreme commander of combined armed forces.

clue.text: Parties appeal to him

parts.note: political parties campaign to win over each person entitled to a vote, so this is a description of a voter

explanation.definitionFit: A voter is the person political parties court at election time.

clue.text: Dash of French?

parts.note: a French word meaning dash or verve, borrowed into English; the surface suggests a small splash of French

explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means flair or vigour, i.e. dash.

clue.text: A toss-up is hard to stop

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for toss is written backwards

parts.note: to lob is to toss high
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Deciding by coin-flip is something that is difficult to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LOB into BOL; the hyphenated 'toss-up' looks like one noun but splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to put an end to something, to stop it altogether.

clue.text: I earn it as a change from work

definitions.text: I earn it as a change from work

indicators.note: change here signals that the letters of the first three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says they earn idleness as a respite from labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges IEARNIT; the whole clue also describes the answer, idleness being a break from work.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggish inactivity, the opposite of doing work.

clue.text: Pass around the mugs

indicators.note: around here means the letters of the first word are moved about

explanation.surface: Hand round the drinking cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass around' reads as a request to hand things round; 'around' rearranges PASS, and 'mugs' means fools, not cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Saps and mugs are both slang for gullible fools.

clue.text: Objecting to baby-sitting?

definitions.meaning: to mind something is to object to it, as in 'do you mind?'
to mind a child is to look after it

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both disliking something and looking after a child.

clue.text: Takes the plunge without consulting the directors

definitions.meaning: to fall from a ship into the sea, or to act with wild excess
read literally, going over the board means bypassing the board of directors

explanation.definitionFit: Literally falling off a ship, and humorously bypassing a company's board.

clue.text: His aim is to see that people settle

definitions.text: His aim is to see that people settle

parts.words: His aim is to see that people settle
parts.note: settle here means pay what they owe, not make a home somewhere

explanation.definitionFit: His job is recovering unpaid money, making people settle their accounts.

clue.text: Seasoning duck with orange, perhaps

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given are not in their final order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Flavouring a duck dish served with orange.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck a l'orange suggests cooking, but 'duck' is O, which joins ORANGE to be rearranged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb used to season food.

clue.text: The cost of having swans in the river

indicators.note: in tells us the swans go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
pens are female swans

explanation.surface: Asking what it costs to keep swans on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Expense is outlay, what something costs.

clue.text: Sound sense of position

indicators.note: Sound at the start says a word is to be heard, not written

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Sound judgement about where one stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound sense' looks like good judgement; 'Sound' signals the homophone of SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or setting, where something is placed.

clue.text: Goodness is a major point in compassion

indicators.note: in places the point inside the word for compassion

parts.note: pity is compassion
E, east, is one of the major points of the compass

explanation.surface: Virtue lies chiefly in showing mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion, a form of virtue.

clue.text: Number clad in gear that's Scottish

indicators.note: clad in means the number is dressed in, so placed inside, the word for gear

parts.note: kit is equipment or clothing
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A garment number worn in Scottish dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a kilt is the item of dress that is Scottish, hinted at by 'gear that's Scottish'.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilt is the tartan skirt traditionally worn by Scotsmen.

clue.text: Turning point upsetting to an eminent person

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the run of letters upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: A crucial moment that unsettles a dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot is the point on which something turns.

clue.text: Delight seen when alto possibly gets top note

indicators.note: gets top means the note is placed above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: possibly signals a rearrangement of the word alto

explanation.surface: A singer is thrilled when the alto hits the top note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ALTO into LOAT; 'seen when' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloat is to delight smugly in something.

clue.text: Application for wood and nails

parts.note: a glossy coating applied to timber, and the same word for the polish put on fingernails

explanation.definitionFit: It is a protective gloss painted on furniture and on fingernails.

clue.text: Term that's musical or legal, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the two words before it are mixed up

explanation.surface: A word that could belong to music or to law.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a tempo marking meaning brisk.

clue.text: Evidence follows concerning blame

indicators.note: follows places the evidence after the word for concerning

parts.note: re means about or concerning
proof is evidence

explanation.surface: Evidence comes next on the question of who is at fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke, an expression of blame.

clue.text: Picnic arranged to entertain upperclass composer

indicators.note: to entertain means to take in a guest, so one piece holds the other
arranged signals a rearrangement of the word picnic

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, as in 'U and non-U'

explanation.surface: An outdoor meal laid on to host a posh composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges PICNIC to PCCINI, which takes in U.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini was the Italian composer of Tosca and La Boheme.

clue.text: A turning point in making a purchase

definitions.text: A turning point in making a purchase

parts.words: A turning point in making a purchase
parts.note: purchase here means leverage, not buying; the clue describes the support on which a lever pivots

explanation.definitionFit: A fulcrum is the pivot that gives a lever its grip or leverage.

clue.text: The Spanish are after an adjustable clasp knife

indicators.note: are after places the Spanish article behind the rearranged letters
adjustable suggests the letters of clasp can be shifted around

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spaniards want an adjustable clasp knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a small surgeon's knife.

clue.text: News item certain favourite comes last

indicators.note: comes last puts the favourite after the word for certain

parts.note: a snip is a certainty, a sure thing
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A news report says a sure-fire favourite finished last.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing a 'snip' is a sure thing, hence 'certain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece of news or information.

clue.text: After the wine I join the company in the porch

indicators.note: after says the letters that follow come after the wine

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: After drinking, I meet the others in the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a columned porch at a building's entrance.

clue.text: A pained expression

parts.note: expression means an utterance, not a look on the face

explanation.definitionFit: It is the exclamation people make when hurt.

clue.text: Clear the area

definitions.meaning: clear in the sense of obvious or evident
a flat expanse of open land

explanation.definitionFit: The word means obvious, and also a flat stretch of open country.

clue.text: Man in hysterics

indicators.note: in says the name sits inside the word hysterics

explanation.surface: A fellow having a fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric is a man's first name.

clue.text: Small yet troublesome inflammation

indicators.note: troublesome signals that the letters of yet are disturbed

explanation.surface: A minor but bothersome swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid.

clue.text: Neighbours provide help with the cleaning

definitions.meaning: Neighbours is a long-running Australian TV serial drama, popular in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: Neighbours is a TV serial drama, and the word is also a washing agent.

clue.text: To carouse is to err drunkenly

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests the letters stagger out of order

explanation.surface: A remark that partying hard is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, to carouse.

clue.text: It may qualify as part of an agreement

definitions.text: It may qualify as part of an agreement

parts.words: It may qualify as part of an agreement
parts.note: qualify means limit or modify, not pass a test; this describes a condition written into a contract

explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Iron out a bottleneck, for example

definitions.text: Iron out a bottleneck, for example

parts.words: Iron out a bottleneck, for example
parts.note: smoothing a narrow neck with an iron combines two incompatible images, an example of muddled figurative speech

explanation.definitionFit: Combining two clashing figures of speech produces this confused imagery.
